title: NSE Leads Rs 24,600 Crore IPO Bonanza With 11 Issues Opening Next Week
excerpt: Eleven IPOs targeting a combined Rs 24,574 crore open for subscription next week, headlined by the NSE's long-awaited Rs 22,569 crore listing — India's second-largest public issue ever — alongside a Rs 1,000 crore Hero Motors offering.
body:
• Eleven IPOs seeking a combined Rs 24,574 crore open for subscription next week, led by the NSE's Rs 22,569 crore offer and Hero Motors' Rs 1,000 crore issue.
  • The NSE's issue opens September 17 and closes September 21, with the price band fixed at Rs 1,700-1,785 per share; the purely secondary offer for sale of 12.64 crore shares was cut by more than 15 percent, with sellers including SBI trimming their stakes.
  • At Rs 22,569 crore, it would be India's second-largest IPO after Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870 crore (2024), surpassing LIC's Rs 21,000 crore (2022); the exchange will list on BSE around September 24.
  • Hero Motors' Rs 1,000 crore IPO opens September 16 at a Rs 79-84 band, valuing the auto-parts maker at Rs 38.15 billion ($401 million), with proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and equipment at its Uttar Pradesh facility.
  • Grey market premiums of about 12 percent for NSE and 11 percent for Hero Motors point to early investor enthusiasm, in a year when 165 Indian IPOs have already raised $8.61 billion, per LSEG data.

India's primary market is heading into one of its busiest weeks of the year: eleven IPOs open for subscription, looking to raise a combined Rs 24,574 crore. Two large mainboard issues — the National Stock Exchange and Hero Motors — account for more than Rs 23,500 crore of the total.

NSE: the decade-long wait ends

The NSE's much-awaited IPO opens for subscription on September 17 and closes on September 21, with anchor investor bidding on September 16. The exchange has fixed a price band of Rs 1,700-1,785 per share for an issue that is entirely an offer for sale of up to 12.64 crore shares by existing shareholders — meaning the proceeds accrue to the sellers, and the exchange itself raises no fresh capital.

The size was cut by more than 15 percent from earlier plans: existing investors including State Bank of India and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board will now sell 126.4 million shares, down from 148.91 million. SBI reduced its proposed sale to about 1.60 crore shares from 2.47 crore, while MS Strategic (Mauritius) cut its offer to 1.1 crore shares from 1.6 crore. Bank of Baroda, Stock Holding Corporation of India and General Insurance Corporation of India also trimmed their sales, and SBI Capital Markets joined as a new selling shareholder.

Reservations run 50 percent for institutional buyers, 15 percent for non-institutional investors and 35 percent for retail; employees get up to Rs 70 crore of shares at a Rs 170 discount. The stock should list on the BSE around September 24 — the NSE did not seek approval to trade its own shares on its own platform — and the exchange is freezing its ISIN from September 11, barring transfers and pledges until listing.

What investors are buying

The NSE is India's largest market infrastructure institution: more than 2,200 listed companies, about $5 trillion in combined market capitalization, roughly 95 percent of cash-equity market share, and the world's largest derivatives exchange by contracts traded. It also runs the benchmark Nifty 50 index. Valued at about $55 billion in the unlisted market, a listing near Rs 1,800 a share would place it among India's ten most valuable companies.

"Post listing NSE will be top 10 among India's largest companies in terms of market cap, which will garner huge interest from the market. At an expected price-to-earnings valuation of around 35 times, the IPO would provide investors with headroom for gains after listing."

— Deven Choksey, Managing Director, DRChoksey FinServ

The issue has been a decade in the making. Founded in 1992, the NSE's listing plans stalled for years amid regulatory hurdles, including the co-location controversy, until Sebi cleared the offering on September 4.

Hero Motors and the rest of the pack

Hero Motors, the BMW- and Ducati-supplying auto-parts maker led by Pankaj Munjal, opens its Rs 1,000 crore IPO on September 16 at Rs 79-84 per share, targeting a Rs 38.15 billion ($401 million) valuation. The sale combines a Rs 6 billion fresh issue with a Rs 4 billion offer for sale; proceeds will trim debt and fund equipment at its Uttar Pradesh facility. ICICI Securities, JM Financial and DAM Capital are the book runners.

Early signals are encouraging: the NSE commands a grey market premium of around 12 percent and Hero Motors about 11 percent. India remains the world's busiest IPO market by number of issues in 2026 — 165 offerings raising $8.61 billion through August 26, per LSEG data — with Jio Platforms' estimated Rs 37,700 crore offering still on the horizon.

What to watch

The anchor book on September 16 will be the first hard read on institutional demand for the NSE, ahead of a likely September 24 listing.
image_caption: The National Stock Exchange building in Mumbai. The NSE's Rs 22,569 crore IPO opens September 17, India's second-largest ever after Hyundai Motor India's 2024 listing.
nri_angle: NRI and OCI investors can participate in Indian IPOs through NRE/NRO accounts under FEMA rules, so the year's headline offerings — including the NSE listing — are directly accessible to the diaspora.
